title: Ambrosian book states: bounded calendar and prayer revisions

traditions.label: Ambrosian Missal
traditions.scope: Historical and reformed Latin source states of Milan; independent translation history deferred.
traditions.coverage_note: Selective, non-exhaustive; dates attest manuscript evidence, publication, approval or effectiveness, never continuous validity. 1913 critical publication, 1990 Italian updated reprint and 2026 Latin publication are not counted as extra reforms. Documented means the stated evidence supports the bounded claim, not a checked native-text transcription. Separate Italian translation history is deferred.

sources.title: BnF FRBNF 36814098: Missale ambrosianum duplex
sources.inspection: Read title, 1913 Milan/Ghirlanda publication, XXIV + 475 pages, Temporal scope and digital holding NUMM-1503133.
sources.limitations: Catalogue establishes the critical edition, not any individual textual delta.

sources.title: Ratti and Magistretti, Missale ambrosianum duplex (1913)
sources.inspection: Gallica item, complete PDF, texteBrut, IIIF and services resolver requests returned 403 in this environment; IA title search found no institutional copy of this critical edition.
sources.limitations: The BnF catalogue establishes 1913 publication and XXIV+475 pages, but no parallel page or apparatus was acquired. 1913 is never treated as a revision date.

sources.title: Jacopo Maria Calloni, La tradizione manoscritta del messale ambrosiano
sources.inspection: Read rendered title page and p. 142: 1751 / 1902 comparison, Ceriani revision project, 1877 permission and manuscript consultation. Screenshot failed.
sources.limitations: Doctoral research; historical overview is not direct inspection of 1751 / 1902 books or the 1877 act. Quoted dates and general account remain source-described.

sources.title: Uwe Michael Lang, Votive Masses of the Holy Face of Christ in Early Printed Diocesan Missals, Mediaeval Studies 79 (2017), 165–203
sources.inspection: Complete publisher PDF acquired. Page 169/PDF 5, including notes 12–13, visually inspected against its page image on 2026-10-17.
sources.limitations: Original comparative research. Its 1475 Veronica attestation is additionally checked in Vatican images; its 1594 removal remains scholarly description because the 1594 original was not inspected. The suggested reason for removal is explicitly probable.

sources.title: Anthony Ward, Modern Ambrosian Prefaces of Saints: Points of Contact with the Roman Missal, Notitiae 32 (1996), 238–267
sources.inspection: Complete official issue acquired, SHA256 ad5dc11915d96ea271fa6da34923ac128a2c4d72f47aec8f469399a707479aca. Article pp 241–244/PDF 63–66 and 266–267/PDF 88–89 visually inspected, including quoted Latin and edition-specific footnotes.
sources.limitations: Image-checking Ward verifies what his article says; it does not independently collate the 1902, 1954 or 1981 altar books. Source-described changes only. Publication in an official journal does not turn scholarship into legislation.

sources.title: Decretum quo Missale Ambrosianum instauratum confirmatur, Prot. 2347/74
sources.inspection: Read complete rendered decree, Notitiae 11 (1975), p. 45, PDF page 19: 30 November 1974 approval of Latin reform.
sources.limitations: Complete decree also image-checked in official 2024 frontmatter, printed IX/PDF 9. Attached approved exemplar remains unavailable; general revision description does not date each prayer change.

sources.title: Dicastery for Divine Worship, Mediolanensis Ecclesia, 7 December 2023, Prot. 183/22
sources.inspection: Read and visually checked complete signed decree printed XI/PDF 11 in official 2024 frontmatter. Approves second Latin typical text and Italian translation; cites Delpini letter 4 November 2022.
sources.limitations: Full decree inspected; attached approved exemplar not available. The previously inspected 2023 Index decretorum p 19 remains corroborating summary.

sources.title: Mario Delpini, complete decree promulgating the second Ambrosian Missal, 28 March 2024
sources.inspection: Read complete decree printed V–VIII; image-checked VI–VIII/PDF 6–8, including signature/seal and dateline 28 March 2024, Prot. Gen. 00822/24; effective 17 November 2024.
sources.limitations: Full official promulgation now inspected. Printed VI gives 32 former Ordinary Time Sundays; publisher advertisement gives 34. Structural facts in the decree do not establish exact Latin prayer wording.

sources.title: ITL Libri, Nuovo Messale Ambrosiano 2024 publication announcement
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF pages 2–3, 5: chronology, named new compositions, calendar and translation changes.
sources.limitations: Publisher account describes Italian publication; check Latin counterparts before attributing individual wording. Page 3 says 34 former Ordinary Time Sundays, conflicting with decree excerpt 32.

sources.title: ITL Libri, Missale Ambrosianum, editio altera
sources.inspection: Read HTML description, 2026 publication, 904 pages, ISBN 9788868948627, replacement of 1981 and shared structural changes.
sources.limitations: Publisher identifies source-recension publication association; no book front matter, complete contents or exact-state identity inspected.

sources.title: Messale Ambrosiano 2024, Premesse/Praenotanda consultation PDF
sources.inspection: Complete 89-page official consultation PDF acquired: 734522 bytes, SHA256 8a1f06caea183819fbcf811aedc07adae29f788187fcd32d29fd2ba4386c7ff2. Colophon PDF 4 and printed VI–IX, XI/PDF 6–9, 11 visually inspected. Full signed 2023 confirmation and 2024 promulgation read.
sources.limitations: Protected modern consultation segment: canonical restricted artifact retains identity and factual loci, no fulltext or images. Entire missal and Latin 2026 book not inspected; no unit-level Latin before/after collation.

sources.title: Missale Ambrosianum 1475, Vatican Inc. III. 420
sources.inspection: Institutional IIIF manifest has 445 canvases. Original ff 35 r–36 r (canvases 76–78) visually inspected: In sancte veronice begins 35 r, Gospel begins Mark 5: 21, proper ends 36 r before In sancte agathe. Images obtained from digi.vatlib.it/iiifimage/Inc.III.420/Inc.III.420_0076_fa_0035r.jp2/full/1500,/0/default.jpg and corresponding 0077/35v and 0078/36r.
sources.limitations: Direct check of this bounded proper, not whole-book collation. February 4 calendar date is still supplied by Lang. Watermarked image derivatives are not redistributed; source claims record exact institutional foliation.

sources.title: USUARIUM 6041, Missale Ambrosianum 1594
sources.inspection: Read Gaspar Visconti title, 1594 date, Alessandrina Roma shelfmark Y g 5, Amiet 0040.
sources.limitations: Different holding from Lang British Library Legg 137; printing equivalence not established. Data attribution: Miklós István Földváry et al., Eötvös Loránd University, USUARIUM, 2015–.

sources.title: Confirmation of Ambrosian Eucharistic prayers for Holy Thursday and Easter Vigil, 1 September 1975, Prot. CD191/75
sources.inspection: Complete 84-page issue acquired, 6619771 bytes, SHA256 93c2c915aeb4e42c24321f9205e3ba8ef4a4b532fa0268ac7b2195cc7c4c5e3f. Printed 346/PDF 64 image-checked under VI. Ritus particulares.
sources.limitations: Official confirmation entry identifies language and liturgical occasions; neither prayer text nor approved exemplar is printed in this entry.

stages.label: Early printed Sanctoral
stages.scope: Selected Sanctoral attestation; not a reconstruction of the entire book.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan, Antonio Zarotto, 1475; British Library IB. 25954; compare Vatican Inc. III. 420.
stages.summary: February 4 Veronica feast and Mass attested.

evidence.claim: Original images directly attest the Veronica proper, Gospel sequence and ending before the Agatha proper.

stages.limitations: Direct original-page reading establishes the bounded proper. Calendar date remains scholarly-described; 1594 removal has not been independently checked. 1499 corroborates this item, not whole-book identity.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Post-Tridentine Sanctoral
stages.scope: Veronica removal only; other revision contents remain unexamined.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan, 1594; British Library Legg 137, described by Lang as Pacifico Da Ponte.
stages.summary: Veronica feast removed in the cited witness.
stages.limitations: Printer differs from Sabbio-labelled catalogue leads; use exact shelfmark and resolve before acquisition. No claim 1594 was the first effective removal.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Pozzobonelli Temporal
stages.scope: Proprium de tempore represented in the 1913 parallel critical edition.
stages.summary: Identified older Temporal state awaiting direct comparison.
stages.limitations: Not a transcription; original 1751 title page and liturgical approval unread.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Ceriani–Ferrari revised missal
stages.scope: Identified typical edition; Temporal and selected Sanctoral preface evidence.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, editio typica, Milan, Agnelli, 1902; Ferrari authority.
stages.summary: Revised state associated with Ceriani manuscript research.
stages.limitations: Full book not read. 1751 → 1902 textual deltas remain uncollated. No 1974 predecessor identity inferred from chronological adjacency.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Approved postconciliar source
stages.scope: Reformed Latin texts approved 30 November 1974; attached exemplar unavailable.
stages.summary: Reform includes Roman-source and newly composed prayers.

evidence.claim: Approves reformed Latin source and describes enrichment.

stages.limitations: Approval is not a 1974 printed book or proof of word-for-word identity with 1981.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Approved special Eucharistic prayers
stages.scope: Latin Ambrosian Eucharistic prayers for Holy Thursday and the Easter Vigil, separately confirmed after the general 1974 approval.
stages.witness_label: Prot. CD191/75, official confirmation entry Notitiae 11 (1975), 346.
stages.summary: A distinct component approval, not evidence of a second whole-missal reform.

evidence.claim: Names the two occasions, Latin language and 1 September 1975 confirmation.

stages.limitations: Prayer texts and attached exemplars not printed in the entry; exact relation to 1981 publication is not text-collated.
stages.reception: Approved Ambrosian use for the two named celebrations; no universal Roman or continuous-unchanged-use claim.

stages.label: First postconciliar Latin book
stages.scope: Published Latin source: selected Sanctoral prefaces described by Ward; calendar organization represented only through the official Latin publisher’s retrospective replacement-and-reorganization account, not a reconstructed calendar.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Mediolani 1981, promulgated under Giovanni Colombo; Ward MA.

evidence.locus: Description: paragraph beginning La pubblicazione della II edizione latina and following principal-changes list, especially La riorganizzazione dell’anno liturgico
evidence.claim: Identifies the first Latin edition of 1981 as the book replaced and describes the successor’s reorganization into seasons after Epiphany and Pentecost. This supplies a retrospective predecessor-calendar scope, without individual 1981 assignments.

stages.limitations: Complete book unavailable in this lane. 1974 approved exemplar and 1975 confirmations not collated; no separate 1981 reform asserted. This publication and the 1974 approval must not be counted as two independently established substantive recensions. Calendar evidence is retrospective and structural only: no 1981 calendar page, feast assignment, Sunday count or precise intermediate source state has been inspected. The evidence does not transfer the Italian 1976/1990 calendar’s exact contents into the Latin 1981 book.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Second reformed source recension
stages.scope: Second Latin typical source and Italian expression; effective 17 November 2024.
stages.witness_label: Latin second typical text approved 7 December 2023; Italian 2024 ISBN 9788868946821; Latin 2026 ISBN 9788868948627.
stages.summary: Reorganized year, updated saints and expanded prayer repertory.

evidence.claim: Approves Latin source and Italian translation.
Associates 2026 Latin publication with second recension.
Separates 1976 first Italian edition, 1986 update, 1990 updated reprint, 2024 second edition; establishes full 2023 approval and 28 March 2024 promulgation with 17 November 2024 effect.

stages.limitations: Complete offered front matter is inspected, but whole 2024 book and 2026 Latin edition are not collated. 1990 is expressly an updated Italian reprint. 2023 approval, 2024 effectiveness and 2026 Latin publication are distinct events of the second recension; no separate reform is inferred from each. Latin loci for the named new propers remain unverified.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

transitions.summary: Veronica feast and proper Mass disappear.

changes.locus_after: 1594 British Library Legg 137; exact page not supplied

transitions.limitations: Source-described, not independent negative search or collation. Intervening editions unreviewed; not an immediate-successor edge. Proposed motivation remains Lang’s probable explanation.

transitions.summary: Older readings were sought through manuscript comparison; exact changed units remain unidentified here.

evidence.claim: Reports Ceriani restoration project and 1913 synopsis.

transitions.limitations: Revision project established, but dossier lacks a checked before/after unit. Do not count this proposal as a demonstrated unit-level transition. 1877 permission is not a complete textual stage; 1913 is not a reform.

transitions.summary: Selected Sanctoral prefaces were replaced, shortened or reordered; related older material also survives in a different genre.

changes.before: Prenatal joy, parental healing and prophetic witness precede naming and sanctification.
changes.after: Moves naming and sanctification first; omits parental-healing clauses.

evidence.claim: Displays predecessor and successor; describes abbreviation and reordering.

changes.before: The older Ambrosian Passion-of-John feast had its own preface.
changes.after: The reformed Passion-of-John preface draws on the modern Roman John-the-Baptist preface, with adaptations and Ambrosian conclusion.
changes.locus_before: Older preface described by Ward pp 241–242

evidence.claim: Describes replacement by the modern Roman-source preface; article pages image-inspected.

changes.before: Sebastian proper used the preface printed 1902 p 330 and 1954 p 465.
changes.after: The Sebastian preface is replaced at 1981 MA 248/6. Related older material, mediated by the modern Roman Common-of-Martyrs preface, appears as an Ambrosian Common-of-Martyrs collect MA483/2; it is not the new Sebastian preface.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes replacement of the Sebastian preface from reuse as a collect elsewhere, and identifies the immediate modern Roman source.

transitions.limitations: Only this preface; no complete-book inheritance or immediate 1902 → 1981 succession. Date of first introduction within postconciliar reform unresolved. Rendered article read; page images failed. Ward p 243 n 12 distinguishes 1902 abstersit from 1954 abstulit; the 1954 quotation must not be silently labeled 1902 wording. Additional Passion-of-John and Sebastian findings remain scholarly-described, with no independent old/new altar-book collation.

transitions.summary: Publication witnesses the approved reform; exact intervening changes unresolved.

evidence.claim: Links earlier approval with 1981 Latin publication.

transitions.limitations: No new substantive 1981 revision claimed and no exact identity certified. 1975 Eucharistic-prayer confirmation needs separate examination.

transitions.summary: Liturgical-year organization and prayer repertory revised.

changes.before: Predecessor calendar organization, known here only from the official Latin publisher’s retrospective replacement-and-reorganization account.
changes.locus_before: ITL Latin 2026 description identifies the 1981 predecessor; its individual calendar pages remain uninspected.

evidence.locus: Description, replacement of the Latin 1981 edition and principal changes, first item
evidence.claim: Connects the reorganized year to the Latin successor of the 1981 edition; does not enumerate the predecessor’s calendar.

changes.after: Expanded Latin prayer repertory; individual added Latin formularies remain uncollated.
changes.locus_before: Earlier edition; individual negative loci not inspected
changes.locus_after: ITL description of the 2026 Latin publication associated with the second recension.

evidence.claim: Latin successor replaces 1981 and receives structural/repertory changes.

Full decree names calendar/lectionary 20 March 2008, saints calendar 27 March 2010, saints lectionary 1 April 2010 and Vigil book 29 June 2015 as intervening changes incorporated in the second missal.

transitions.limitations: Full 2023 confirmation and 2024 promulgation now checked; exact before/after Latin prayer units remain uncollated. The decree explicitly retrospectively identifies 2008, 2010 and 2015 component changes: they are not asserted to be separate whole-missal editions. 2020 Italian translation changes are not independent Latin source revisions. Sunday-count discrepancy 32 (decree) versus 34 (publisher) remains explicit.

gaps.next_source: BL IB. 25954 ff. 35 r–36 r; BL Legg 137; Alessandrina Y g 5 (Usuarium 6041); BnF 1594 Sabbio record.
gaps.consequence: Removal is a scoped scholarly claim, not a complete 1475 → 1594 → 1751 chain.

gaps.missing: Exact Latin before/after units and original 2008/2010/2015 component books. Full 2023 decree, 2024 frontmatter and promulgation are acquired and inspected; 1990 is now verified as updated reprint. Named Joseph 16 December, second Trinity preface and Church-from-the-nations Mass still require exact Latin loci.
gaps.next_source: Original Latin 1981 and 2026 altar-book contents and named changed loci; separate 2008 calendar/lectionary, 2010 saints calendar/lectionary and 2015 Vigil book. Official 2024 frontmatter printed VI supplies exact promulgation dates and scope.
gaps.consequence: Second-recension structural changes have full-act evidence; no exact Latin wording, complete diff or extra reform for each publication/reprint is inferred.

gaps.missing: Original 1902, 1954 and 1981 altar-book image comparison and independent 1594 removal check. Langp 169 and Ward pp 241–244, 266–267 scholarly images are now checked; 1475 Veronica originals are checked.
gaps.next_source: Institutional originals of the specific altar-book editions and loci named by Lang and Ward; the remaining task is original-to-original comparison, not another OCR check of the articles.

gaps.period: Postconciliar reform, attested in the 1981 Latin book
gaps.missing: Original-book verification of the now image-checked Ward descriptions of the Passion-of-John replacement and Sebastian/common-martyrs genre transfer.
gaps.next_source: Anthony Ward, Notitiae 32 (1996), pp. 241–242 and 266–267; source ambrosian-ward-1996. The Passion-of-John preface adapts Roman 1970 material. Two distinct Sebastian-related operations require comparison: replacement of the older Sebastian preface (1902 p. 330; 1954 p. 465) at MA 248/6, and recasting related material through the postconciliar Roman preface into the Common of Martyrs collect at MA 483/2. The Common collect is not the replacement Sebastian preface.
gaps.consequence: Potential additional bounded comparisons within an existing transition, not additional stages or completed collations.
